body.name: robust heavy-light interval handle
body.construction:
Set
\[
 \widehat{\mathcal L}
 =\left\{k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}:
       \min_{a\in\{0,1\}}N_{ak}^{(0)}\le256\log(en)\right\}.
\]
On the event \(\widehat{\mathcal L}=\varnothing\), discard the light branch by
setting \(\widehat T_{\mathrm L}=\widehat R_{\mathrm L}=0\), and impose the exact
sample identities
\[
 (\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}})
 =(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}},\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}).
\]
On \(\widehat{\mathcal L}\ne\varnothing\), retain the pilot-selected
four-coordinate factorial lift on \(\widehat{\mathcal L}\) and the proposed
saturated treated--control ratio and within-cell fourth-moment truncation
recipe on its complement to produce candidate sample-measurable outputs
\(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}\) and \(\widehat V^{\mathrm{HL}}\).  Treat
\(\widehat R_{\mathrm L}\) and the heavy-score component entering
\(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}\) only as proposed sample-measurable outputs; this
definition asserts no finite-sample tail, coverage, or expected-radius
certificate for them.  Truncate \(\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}\) to
\([0,2M]\), and for every sample return
\[
 \widehat C^{\mathrm{HL}}
 = [\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}-\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}},
    \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{HL}}+\widehat R^{\mathrm{HL}}]
    \cap[-2M,2M].
\]
